tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in messages from the system in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. """The ``pennywise`` command line."""

import argparse
import csv
import io
import json
import os
import sys

from .ledger import (
    Entry,
    ParseError,
    check_amount,
    check_category,
    check_date,
    format_amount,
    format_entry,
    parse,
    split_lines,
    strip_bom,
)
from .reports import balance, by_category, by_month, filter_entries


class _Fail(Exception):
    def __init__(self, code, message):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.code = code
        self.message = message


def _date_arg(text):
    try:
        return check_date(text)
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise argparse.ArgumentTypeError(str(exc)) from None


def _read_text(path):
    if path == "-":
        if sys.stdin is None:
            raise _Fail(2, "cannot read standard input")
        try:
            # Decode the raw bytes strictly, like a file, whatever the locale's
            # error handler says; a stream without a buffer is already text.
            buffer = getattr(sys.stdin, "buffer", None)
            if buffer is None:
                return sys.stdin.read()
            return buffer.read().decode("utf-8")
        except (OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            raise _Fail(2, "cannot read standard input: {}".format(exc)) from None
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
            return handle.read()
    except OSError as exc:
        raise _Fail(2, "cannot read {}: {}".format(path, exc.strerror or exc)) from None
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise _Fail(2, "cannot read {}: {}".format(path, exc)) from None


def _load(path):
    try:
        return parse(_read_text(path))
    except ParseError as exc:
        raise _Fail(1, str(exc)) from None


def _sorted_entries(entries):
    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: e.date)


def _json(value):
    return json.dumps(value) + "\n"


def _lines(lines):
    return "".join(line + "\n" for line in lines)


def _cmd_balance(args):
    total = format_amount(balance(_load(args.file)))
    if args.json:
        return _json({"balance": total})
    return total + "\n"


def _cmd_summary(args):
    entries = _load(args.file)
    totals = by_month(entries) if args.by == "month" else by_category(entries)
    shown = {name: format_amount(totals[name]) for name in sorted(totals)}
    if args.json:
        return _json(shown)
    return _lines("{}  {}".format(name, total) for name, total in shown.items())


def _selected(args):
    entries = filter_entries(
        _load(args.file),
        category=getattr(args, "category", None),
        since=getattr(args, "since", None),
        until=getattr(args, "until", None),
    )
    return _sorted_entries(entries)


def _cmd_list(args):
    entries = _selected(args)
    if args.json:
        return _json(
            [
                {
                    "date": e.date.isoformat(),
                    "category": e.category,
                    "amount": format_amount(e.amount),
                    "note": e.note,
                }
                for e in entries
            ]
        )
    return _lines(format_entry(e) for e in entries)


def _cmd_export(args):
    out = io.StringIO()
    writer = csv.writer(out, lineterminator="\n")
    writer.writerow(["date", "category", "amount", "note"])
    for e in _selected(args):
        writer.writerow([e.date.isoformat(), e.category, format_amount(e.amount), e.note])
    return out.getvalue()


def _line_count(text):
    if not text:
        return 0
    lines = split_lines(text)
    return len(lines) - 1 if lines[-1] == "" else len(lines)


def _cmd_add(args):
    if args.file == "-":
        raise _Fail(2, "add does not accept '-' (give a file name)")
    try:
        with open(args.file, encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
            existing = handle.read()
    except FileNotFoundError:
        existing = ""
    except OSError as exc:
        raise _Fail(2, "cannot read {}: {}".format(args.file, exc.strerror or exc)) from None
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise _Fail(2, "cannot read {}: {}".format(args.file, exc)) from None

    number = _line_count(existing) + 1
    note = (args.note or "").strip()
    try:
        date = check_date(args.date)
        category = check_category(args.category)
        amount = check_amount(args.amount)
        if "\n" in note or "\r" in note:
            raise ValueError("invalid note (must not contain a newline)")
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise _Fail(1, "line {}: {}".format(number, exc)) from None

    line = format_entry(Entry(date, category, amount, note))
    body = strip_bom(existing)
    prefix = "\n" if body and not body.endswith(("\n", "\r")) else ""
    try:
        with open(args.file, "a", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
            handle.write(prefix + line + "\n")
    except OSError as exc:
        raise _Fail(2, "cannot write {}: {}".format(args.file, exc.strerror or exc)) from None
    return line + "\n"


def _build_parser():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="pennywise", description="Tell me where the household money went."
    )
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", metavar="COMMAND")
    sub.required = True

    def reader(name, help_text):
        p = sub.add_parser(name, help=help_text, description=help_text)
        p.add_argument("file", metavar="FILE", help="ledger file, or - for standard input")
        return p

    p = reader("balance", "print the total of all amounts")
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_balance)

    p = reader("summary", "print totals per category or month")
    p.add_argument("--by", choices=["category", "month"], default="category")
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_summary)

    def filters(p):
        p.add_argument("--category", help="only this category (any case)")
        p.add_argument("--since", type=_date_arg, metavar="DATE", help="from DATE, inclusive")
        p.add_argument("--until", type=_date_arg, metavar="DATE", help="up to DATE, inclusive")

    p = reader("list", "print entries, oldest first")
    filters(p)
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="print JSON")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_list)

    p = reader("export", "print entries as CSV, in list order")
    p.add_argument("--format", choices=["csv"], default="csv")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_export)

    p = sub.add_parser("add", help="append an entry to a ledger file", description="append an entry")
    p.add_argument("file", metavar="FILE")
    p.add_argument("date", metavar="DATE")
    p.add_argument("category", metavar="CATEGORY")
    p.add_argument("amount", metavar="AMOUNT")
    p.add_argument("note", metavar="NOTE", nargs="?", default="")
    p.set_defaults(func=_cmd_add)
    return parser


def _complain(message):
    if sys.stderr is None:
        return
    try:
        sys.stderr.write("pennywise: {}\n".format(message))
        sys.stderr.flush()
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        pass


def main(argv=None):
    """Run the command line; return the exit status."""
    try:
        args = _build_parser().parse_args(argv)
    except SystemExit as exc:
        code = exc.code
        return 0 if code is None else code
    try:
        output = args.func(args)
    except _Fail as exc:
        _complain(exc.message)
        return exc.code
    if sys.stdout is None:
        # Standard output is closed (e.g. `>&-`): nowhere to print.
        _complain("cannot write standard output")
        return 2
    try:
        sys.stdout.write(output)
        sys.stdout.flush()
    except BrokenPipeError:
        # The reader closed the pipe early (e.g. `| head -1`). Point stdout at
        # devnull so the flush at interpreter exit cannot fail again, and end quietly.
        try:
            os.dup2(os.open(os.devnull, os.O_WRONLY), sys.stdout.fileno())
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            pass
    return 0

Issue #11 is fixed and PR #27 is squash-merged. The command from the issue (`PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii pennywise list u8.txt`) now prints `2024-01-01 a 1.00 café` and exits 0, with no traceback.

- **Approach:** All stdout output is written as UTF-8 whatever the locale. This follows the issue's first option, since the ledger is UTF-8 too. The change is a small `_write_stdout` helper in `src/pennywise/cli.py`, and the README now documents it.
- **Tests:** I added three tests in `tests/test_cli.py`. They check `list`, `export`, `summary` and `add` under `PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii`, `latin-1` and `LC_ALL=C`. A fourth check runs in-process against an ASCII text stream. With the source change stashed and the tests kept, all three fail; with the change, they pass.
- **Test run:** I ran `tests.test_cli`, `tests.test_ledger` and `tests.test_reports` together. That is 90 tests, all passing. `rtdd which` listed the new tests, but I ran the unittest modules directly rather than rtdd's own Round 1 and Round 2 commands.

- **Merge:** Nothing had landed on `main` since my branch, so I skipped the rebase.

I don't know whether Windows newline handling works. The helper writes bytes and swaps `\n` for `os.linesep` itself, and I only ran on Linux.
